prompt:
Postgres 13, self-hosted, and we can't upgrade this year. This query comes from our Java service via JDBC prepared statements:

SELECT id, status, total
FROM orders
WHERE region = ? AND status IN ('NEW','PAID') AND created_at > now() - interval '1 day'
ORDER BY created_at DESC
LIMIT 50;

orders has 80M rows, 12 regions, NEW+PAID are ~3% of all rows, ~20k new orders/day per region. ~400 QPS on this query, ~300 inserts/sec, each order's status is updated 1-2 times.
Existing indexes: orders_pkey (id), idx_orders_region (region), idx_orders_created (created_at).

What index should I add, and how do I see the plan the app actually gets (not just what psql shows me)?
assertions: The recommended index has region first and created_at (DESC) right after it, with status handled by a partial index predicate (WHERE status IN ('NEW','PAID')) or placed after created_at
The response explains why status IN ('NEW','PAID') should not sit between region and created_at (multi-value IN breaks the order / forces a sort), or why a partial index removes it from the key
The response does not present EXPLAIN (GENERIC_PLAN) as available on PostgreSQL 13; if mentioned, it is flagged as PostgreSQL 16+ only
The response gives a PostgreSQL 13-valid way to see the app's real plan: PREPARE/EXECUTE 6+ times, SET plan_cache_mode = force_generic_plan, and/or auto_explain with log_analyze
The response mentions JDBC server-side prepare behavior (prepareThreshold, default 5) or otherwise explains when the driver switches to a server-prepared / generic plan
The response does not rely on B-tree skip scan (PostgreSQL 18+) for the recommendation
The response uses CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY
The response addresses write cost given ~300 inserts/sec and 1-2 status updates per order (e.g. partial index entries added/removed on status change, HOT updates)
The response addresses the existing idx_orders_region / idx_orders_created (redundant or to evaluate dropping)
The response gives EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) and describes what a good plan looks like (no Sort, index scan feeding Limit)
